correctness.rationale: The exact gap polynomial is reconstructed from the previous-occurrence dynamic recurrence and nilpotent zero-block matrix. Pair-gap smoothing has strict positive differences whenever imbalanced by at least two. Four explicit algebraic transfer differences and parity comparisons provide the exact all-n equality cases. A direct-subsequence-set checker on 330 small words and a dynamic checker over 73,815 quadruples confirm the formulas; finite tests are not invoked as an infinite proof.

evidence: Flaxman–Harrow–Sorkin Theorem 2 maximizes over all binary words at each length, uniquely producing a length-n alternating pattern; it gives an exponential Fibonacci optimum.
Liron–Langberg Theorem III.1 optimizes for fixed number of nonempty runs, with balanced equal-run lengths only when divisible; these balancing moves need not preserve the count of ones.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted Fibonacci bound is not tight for weight three for increasing n; its optimizer lies outside the specified class. Balanced-run bounds do not select a fixed-three-ones maximizing word or derive the exact quartic. Therefore their stronger-looking optimization domains do not logically give this constrained answer.

value.rationale: Fixed Hamming weight is a natural deletion-channel source constraint. This all-length optimum and full optimizer classification refine the classical unrestricted Fibonacci maximum into an exact quartic composition-restricted extremum, with an explicit and structurally motivated balancing mechanism. The result is not merely a fixed small table or a routine substitution of a published bound.
